guidance.heading: OUTLOOK
section: The Company continues its pursuit of a joint venture agreement on the KSM Project with a senior mining company partner that has technical, financial, and social capabilities to support development of the Project. The KSM Project includes multiple deposits and development scenarios that provide a joint venture partner flexibility in the design of the Project.
Planned activities through the balance of 2026 on the KSM project include:

•Continuation of FS activities, including engineering, to support the initiation of a FS which remains targeted for completion by the end of 2027. Engineering studies work includes the completion of trade off studies and preparation of the design criteria for the proposed FS.
•Environmental monitoring and technical studies covering activities required to prepare for the FS, and future permitting applications.
•Maintaining site camps, site operations, permits and social outreach programs, including Indigenous partner engagements.
Other Project works that have been largely concluded for the season and were successful in achieving the planned 2026 work scope, include:

•The FS site investigation included the most significant geotechnical program ever completed at the KSM site, with drilling programs in the Treaty and Mitchell valleys, and in the proposed process and tailings management area ("PTMA"). The program completed a total of 177 drill holes and 211 test pits, along with numerous geophysical programs. Drillholes provided geotechnical and hydrogeology data, as well as samples for metallurgical and geochemical testing.

•Completion of 13 kilometers of Upper Treaty Creek Access Road (“UTCAR”) to provide access to the site of the MTT saddle portal access. BC Hydro has substantially completed work on the TCT, a key component of the system required to provide power from the Northwest Transmission Line ("NTL”) for use during construction and operations.

At the Bronson Corridor Project, Seabridge's exploration program is focused on better defining new targets through enhanced surface geochemical sampling and geological mapping on untested and underexplored targets on the property. Additional evaluation of the historical core was undertaken to better understand mineral distribution and relationship to intrusive centers. Results from these ongoing evaluations are currently pending and will help guide future exploration activities.
Executing this more limited program has also resulted in a pause of the voluntary reclamation program at the Johnny Mountain Mine.

desk.headline: No revenue (development company); small C$6.7m profit on a non-cash note gain; cash down to C$56m, US$100m loan fully drawn; KSM feasibility study still targeted for end-2027

other.label: Loan facility drawn
other.change: US$50m at 30 Sep, rest on 2 Nov; due by 31 Dec 2026

results: Seabridge has no revenue; the C$6.7m quarterly profit came mainly from a C$16.2m non-cash gain on revaluing its secured notes.
Spending on mineral properties, mostly the KSM project, rose to C$90.2m in the quarter from C$52.9m a year ago.
Cash fell to C$56.3m from C$117.5m at end-2025, while current liabilities rose to C$140.1m.
A new US$100m unsecured loan from a strategic investor (7% interest) is fully drawn and due by 31 Dec 2026, payable in cash or shares.
Holders of the secured notes can demand about US$412m from March 2028 (puts payable in cash or shares).

guidance.summary: No financial guidance. The company is still seeking a senior mining partner for a KSM joint venture and targets a KSM feasibility study by end-2027.

points: Management keeps pursuing a joint venture on KSM with a large mining company.
The 2026 site season is largely done, including the biggest geotechnical drill programme ever at KSM.
13 km of access road was completed and BC Hydro has largely finished the Treaty Creek power terminal.
Exploration at Bronson Corridor was scaled back, pausing voluntary reclamation at the old Johnny Mountain mine.
